subject: geography
title: Ecosystems Adventure: Rainforests at Risk
welcome_lead: The Amazon is being cleared at the rate of a football pitch a minute. Why — and what can stop it?
meta_desc: GCSE Geography tropical rainforest case study — Amazon, deforestation, sustainable management.
final_note: You learned the causes and impacts of deforestation and how to manage rainforests sustainably.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Rainforest soil is surprisingly POOR — heavy rain washes nutrients out.

The forest survives via a rapid nutrient cycle: dead leaves rot in days, releasing nutrients straight back to trees. Remove the trees and the soil dies.

Causes of deforestation:

Cattle ranching (~70% of clearance in Brazilian Amazon).
Soya farming for animal feed.
Logging for hardwoods.
Mining (iron, gold).
Roads (Trans-Amazonian Highway) open up new land.
Brazil has lost ~17% of its Amazon since 1970.

Selective logging: only mature trees taken — canopy survives.

Replanting and agroforestry mix trees with crops.

Ecotourism: small-scale tourism funds conservation (Costa Rica is a leader).

International agreements: REDD+ pays countries to protect forest.

mcqs.q: What is the BIGGEST single cause of deforestation in the Brazilian Amazon?
options: Mining
Cattle ranching
Hydropower dams
Subsistence farming

mcqs.q: Why is the SOIL in a tropical rainforest typically infertile if the trees are removed?
options: It is too cold
Heavy rain leaches nutrients without trees to cycle them
It is too dry
The soil is too rocky

mcqs.q: Why does deforestation increase flood risk?
options: Deforestation causes floods because trees normally hold water in their branches forever.
Deforestation has no effect on rivers — only rainfall matters.
Because HDI is easier to calculate than GNI.
Trees intercept rainfall, their roots increase infiltration and transpiration removes water — removing them increases surface runoff and reduces lag time, peaking river levels faster.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between biotic and abiotic components of an ecosystem?
options: Because HDI is easier to calculate than GNI.
Biotic means animals and abiotic means plants.
Biotic and abiotic both refer to types of soil.
Biotic components are all living organisms (plants, animals, microbes); abiotic components are non-living factors (climate, soil, water, light, rock).
